conceptual assets.concept: Register write-back data (value written into the register file)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The value written into the architectural register file is formed and driven inside this entity: 'rf_wdata <= alu_res or lsu_rdata or csr_rdata or ctrl.pc_ret;' and the regfile instance receives it via 'neorv32_cpu_regfile_inst ... rd_i => rf_wdata'. Corruption of this stored write-back value or its computed sources breaks register contents and downstream execution; rf_wdata is the stored writeback value and alu_res/lsu_rdata/csr_rdata/ctrl.pc_ret are its defining sources.

conceptual assets.concept: Control CSR command and data signals (CSR write/read enables, address, write-data)
conceptual assets.reasoning: Control produces CSR command fields which drive CSR access logic: the control block exports 'ctrl' (neorv32_cpu_control_inst port map ctrl_o => ctrl) and the ICC block consumes those fields (neorv32_cpu_icc_inst port map csr_we_i => ctrl.csr_we, csr_re_i => ctrl.csr_re, csr_addr_i => ctrl.csr_addr, csr_wdata_i => ctrl.csr_wdata). Incorrect ctrl.csr_* values would perform wrong CSR operations, establishing an Integrity requirement.

conceptual assets.concept: CSR read-data aggregated and returned to control (xcsr_res)
conceptual assets.reasoning: CSR readback seen by the control block is assembled here: 'xcsr_res <= xcsr_cnt or xcsr_alu or xcsr_pmp or xcsr_icc' and the control instance receives it via 'neorv32_cpu_control_inst ... xcsr_rdata_i => xcsr_res'. Corruption of these CSR read-data signals would present incorrect CSR values to control, violating integrity of CSR reads.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt inputs consumed by control (debug, machine software/external/timer, fast IRQs)
conceptual assets.reasoning: Interrupt sources are provided to the control block and determine interrupt handling: 'irq_machine <= mti_i & mei_i & msi_i' and neorv32_cpu_control_inst maps irq_machine_i => irq_machine, irq_fast_i => firq_i and irq_dbg_i => dbi_i. If these input signals or the assembled irq_machine vector are tampered with, control will make incorrect interrupt decisions; the RTL explicitly wires the inputs into control.

conceptual assets.concept: PMP fault indicator reported to control (pmp_fault)
conceptual assets.reasoning: When PMP is enabled the PMP unit drives 'pmp_fault' (neorv32_cpu_pmp port map fault_o => pmp_fault) and when disabled the RTL drives pmp_fault <= '0'; the control instance consumes this signal via 'pmp_fault_i => pmp_fault'. Corrupting pmp_fault would misreport memory-protection faults to control, violating integrity of fault reporting.

conceptual assets.concept: Load/store unit results and status consumed by core (lsu_rdata, lsu_wait, lsu_err, lsu_mar)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The LSU produces load data and status that the core depends on: neorv32_cpu_lsu port map rdata_o => lsu_rdata, wait_o => lsu_wait, err_o => lsu_err, mar_o => lsu_mar. lsu_rdata feeds write-back ('rf_wdata <= ... or lsu_rdata'), and lsu_wait/lsu_err/lsu_mar are forwarded to control. Integrity of load data and error reporting is required for correct architectural state; availability of lsu_wait is also required for correct stalling behavior (noted in reasoning).

conceptual assets.concept: ALU outputs used for writeback and control decisions (alu_res, alu_cmp, alu_add)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The ALU instance produces results and comparison/add outputs used by write-back and control: neorv32_cpu_alu_inst port map cmp_o => alu_cmp, res_o => alu_res, add_o => alu_add. alu_res is a write-back source (rf_wdata), and alu_cmp/alu_add are input to control (alu_cmp_i, alu_add_i). Incorrect ALU outputs will cause wrong computation and incorrect control decisions, establishing Integrity.

conceptual assets.concept: Register-file source operands (rs1, rs2, rs3) consumed by execution units
conceptual assets.reasoning: The regfile instance exports architectural operand values: neorv32_cpu_regfile_inst port map rs1_o => rs1, rs2_o => rs2, rs3_o => rs3, and the ALU/LSU consume these (neorv32_cpu_alu_inst rs1_i/rs2_i/rs3_i => rs1/rs2/rs3; neorv32_cpu_lsu_inst wdata_i => rs2). Integrity of these stored register outputs is required for correct instruction execution.
